title: Saying Sorry Well: The Four Parts of a Real Apology
description: A real apology has four parts: say what happened, say it was wrong, say how you'll fix it, and ask for forgiveness — without the word 'but'.

body.heading: 'Sorry' is a start, not the whole thing
paragraphs: Everyone says sorry. But some apologies heal, and some just make noise. The difference is not talent — it is parts. A real apology has four of them, and leaving one out is like bringing a stool with a missing leg.

body.heading: Part 1 and 2: name it, own it
paragraphs: Part 1 — Say what you did. 'I knocked your tower down.' Not 'sorry about… the thing.' Naming it proves you know what hurt.
Part 2 — Say it was wrong, without excuses. 'That was wrong of me.' Watch out for the word BUT: 'I'm sorry, but you were in the way' quietly erases the whole apology.

body.heading: Part 3 and 4: fix it, ask
paragraphs: Part 3 — Say how you will fix it or do better. 'I will help you rebuild it, and I will walk around your work from now on.' A fix can be an action, a repair, or a real plan.
Part 4 — Ask, don't demand. 'Will you forgive me?' The other person may need time. Asking and then respecting their answer is part of the apology too.

body.heading: What a real apology sounds like
paragraphs: Put together: 'I knocked your tower down when I ran past. That was careless and wrong of me. I will help you rebuild it now, and I will walk in the classroom from today. Will you forgive me?'
It takes twenty seconds. It also takes courage — which is exactly why it works.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Think of a 'sorry' you once received that did NOT feel real. Which part was missing?
2. Why do you think Part 4 says 'ask, don't demand'? What happens to an apology when forgiveness is demanded?

takeaway: A real apology has four parts — name what you did, own that it was wrong (no 'but'), say how you'll fix it, and ask for forgiveness while respecting the answer.
